chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Mansour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one who does not fast during Dhu al-Hijjah until the crescent of Muharram is seen, upon him is the blood of a sheep, and it is not for him to fast, and he should slaughter it at Mina.

key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: Blood of a sheep (sacrificial animal penalty)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.هِلَالُ الْمُحَرَّمِ: The crescent of Muharram (marking the start of the new month)

ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for a pilgrim who hasn't fasted Dhu al-Hijjah before Muharram?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* specifies the *dam* (sacrificial animal) penalty for a pilgrim who delays fasting until after the Muharram crescent is sighted, a condition often linked to the *Tamattu'* Hajj type where the fast is postponed. The requirement to slaughter the sheep in Mina underscores the geographical sanctity of the penalty, aligning with the broader Hajj rituals of sacrifice. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on timely fulfillment of fasting obligations during the Hajj period to avoid additional expiation.
